Catholic Schools Inspectorate
Catholic Schools Inspectorate (CSI) Report
At St John Fisher Catholic Primary School, we are proud of our strong Catholic identity and our commitment to nurturing children in faith, learning and personal growth.
Catholic Schools Inspectorate (CSI) inspections evaluate how effectively Catholic schools fulfil their mission and support the spiritual, moral and educational development of pupils.
The inspection considers important aspects of school life including:
Catholic Life and Mission
How effectively the school promotes Gospel values, Catholic identity, relationships, inclusion and service.
The quality of Religious Education teaching, learning, curriculum provision and pupil progress.
How children participate in and contribute to prayer, worship, reflection, and the spiritual life of the school.
At St John Fisher, we are proud of our faith-filled community where children are encouraged to grow in wisdom, compassion, confidence and courage.
Our CSI inspection reflects our dedication to living out our mission each day:
“We stand united in faith with the courage to build a loving world of truth, justice, peace and wisdom.”

pageCache.text:
Catholic Ethos Statement
Our Catholic Ethos
At St John Fisher Catholic Primary School, our Catholic ethos is at the heart of everything we do. It shapes our relationships, our curriculum, our decision-making and the daily experiences of every child.
Inspired by the teachings of Jesus Christ and the example of St John Fisher, we are committed to creating a loving, inclusive and faith-filled environment where every child is known, valued and encouraged to flourish.
Our mission guides all aspects of school life:
“We stand united in faith with the courage to build a loving world of truth, justice, peace and wisdom.”
This mission inspires us to nurture children who are spiritually aware, academically successful, emotionally resilient, socially responsible and morally grounded.
Living Our Catholic Ethos
Our Catholic ethos is lived each day through:
Prayer, worship, Gospel values and reflection are woven into everyday school life.
We encourage children to treat one another with kindness, dignity, forgiveness and respect.
We believe every child is created in the image of God and gifted with unique talents and potential.
Children are encouraged to care for others, support charitable causes and make a positive difference within their communities.
Community and Togetherness
Strong partnerships between school, family, parish and the wider community help children flourish.
Our LIGHT Values
Our ethos is reflected in our LIGHT values:
Love - showing kindness, compassion and respect Integrity - acting with honesty, fairness and responsibility Growth - striving to learn, improve and persevere Hope - tusting in God’s plan and looking to the future with optimism Togetherness - working as one family united in faith and purpose
At St John Fisher, we want every child to leave us with a lifelong love of learning, a strong moral compass, and the confidence to shine brightly in the world.
When children feel loved, inspired and supported, they flourish.

Prayer and Collective Worship
Prayer and collective worship are central to life at St John Fisher Catholic Primary School. They provide opportunities for children, staff and the wider school community to come together in faith, reflection, celebration and spiritual growth.
As a Catholic school, prayer and worship are rooted in the teachings of Christ and guided by our mission:
“We stand united in faith with the courage to build a loving world of truth, justice, peace and wisdom.”
We believe worship should be meaningful, inclusive and inspiring, helping children develop a deeper relationship with God and a stronger understanding of faith in everyday life.
Our Approach to Prayer and Collective Worship
Prayer and collective worship at St John Fisher aim to:
Children experience a variety of prayer opportunities including:
We encourage pupils to become active participants in planning and leading worship so they grow in confidence and spiritual understanding.
Develop children’s relationship with God
Encourage reflection, gratitude and compassion
Celebrate important liturgical seasons and feast days
Build a sense of belonging and community
Whole school worship
Child-led prayer experiences
Celebration of Mass
Reflection linked to scripture and Gospel values
Prayer during key liturgical seasons

pageCache.pageTitle: St John Fisher Catholic Primary School - Catholic Social Teaching
pageCache.text:
Catholic Social Teaching
At St John Fisher Catholic Primary School, our Catholic faith calls us to love God and love our neighbour in every situation. Inspired by the teachings of Jesus, we encourage our children to recognise their responsibility to care for others, stand up for justice and make a positive difference in the world.
Catholic Social Teaching (CST) is rooted in Scripture and developed through the wisdom of the Church. It provides a moral framework that helps us understand how we can live out our faith in everyday life and respond to the needs of others with compassion, dignity and love.
As Jesus teaches us:
"Love your neighbour as yourself."
At St John Fisher, Catholic Social Teaching is not something we only learn about - it is something we live.
We help children understand that they are called to be active citizens who care for the world and the people in it. Through prayer, charity, fundraising, pupil leadership, community projects, worship, and our curriculum, children learn how faith can inspire action.
Our Catholic Social Teaching Principles
We draw upon the principles of Catholic Social Teaching, including:
Every person is created in the image and likeness of God and deserves love, dignity and respect.
We work together to help everyone flourish and contribute positively to society.
Everyone has a role to play in creating a fair and loving world.
Option for the Poor and Vulnerable
We are called to care especially for those most in need.
Stewardship of Creation
We have a responsibility to care for God’s world and protect the environment.
Solidarity and Peace
We recognise that we are one human family and are called to live with compassion, justice and peace.
Every person deserves respect, fairness, and opportunity.
Inspired by the teachings of the Church, including Pope Leo XIV and previous Catholic leaders, Catholic Social Teaching continues to help us understand how faith should shape our actions in an ever-changing world.
At St John Fisher, we strive to live these principles each day as we work together to build “a loving world of truth, justice, peace and wisdom.”

pageCache.pageTitle: St John Fisher Catholic Primary School - Mission Statement
pageCache.text:
Mission Statement
“We stand united in faith with the courage to build a loving world of truth, justice, peace and wisdom.”
At St John Fisher Catholic Primary School, our mission statement lies at the heart of everything we do. It expresses who we are as a Catholic school community and reflects our commitment to nurturing children in faith, learning, and love.
Inspired by the teachings of Christ and the example of St John Fisher, our mission guides the decisions we make, the relationships we build, and the experiences we provide for every child.
We believe education is about far more than academic success alone. Our aim is to help children flourish spiritually, academically, socially, emotionally, and morally so that they grow into confident, compassionate, and responsible young people.
Our mission calls us to:
Stand united in faith
Faith is central to life at St John Fisher. Through prayer, worship, Gospel values and everyday relationships, we help children develop a personal relationship with God and an understanding of what it means to live as part of a loving Catholic community.
Live with courage
We encourage children to be resilient, hopeful and confident in facing challenges. We want our pupils to have the courage to stand up for what is right, embrace opportunities and use their gifts to make a positive difference.
Build a loving world
Love is at the foundation of all we do. We teach children to care for others, celebrate differences, show compassion and contribute positively to their communities.
Seek truth, justice, peace and wisdom
Through our curriculum, relationships, and Catholic life, we help children understand the importance of honesty, fairness, forgiveness, respect and thoughtful decision-making.
Our mission is lived each day through our motto:
“When you love to learn, you learn to love.”
Together, we are building a school community where children grow in faith and learning, guided by light and courage, to shape a loving and just world.

pageCache.pageTitle: St John Fisher Catholic Primary School - Our Values
pageCache.text:
Our Values
At St John Fisher Catholic Primary School, our values are at the heart of everything we do. They shape our relationships, guide our decisions, and help us create a community where every child feels known, valued, and inspired to flourish.
Inspired by the teachings of Christ and rooted in our Catholic faith, our values remind us that education is about nurturing hearts as well as minds. Alongside academic excellence, we are committed to helping children develop character, confidence, compassion, and a strong sense of purpose.
Our values spell LIGHT, reminding us that Christ’s light shines through all that we do.
Love
We show kindness, compassion, dignity and respect to everyone in our school community.
Love is the foundation of St John Fisher. We teach children to care for one another, celebrate differences, and build relationships rooted in empathy, forgiveness and understanding. Through love, children learn to value themselves and others as unique individuals created in the image of God.
Integrity
We act with honesty, fairness and responsibility.
We encourage children to make good choices, take responsibility for their actions, and always strive to do what is right - even when it may be difficult. Integrity helps our children become trustworthy, reflective and respectful individuals who understand the importance of truth and justice.
Growth
We strive to learn, improve and persevere every day.
At St John Fisher, we believe every child can succeed. We encourage children to embrace challenge, develop resilience and take pride in their achievements. Growth means recognising that mistakes are part of learning and understanding that effort, determination and perseverance help us to become the very best version of ourselves.
Hope
We trust in God’s plan and look to the future with optimism.
Hope inspires us to remain positive, resilient and ambitious. We want our children to believe in themselves, aim high and face challenges with courage and confidence. Through faith and encouragement, children learn that they can make a positive difference in the world around them.
Togetherness
We work as one family, united in faith and purpose.
We believe strong relationships are central to success. At St John Fisher, children, staff, families, parish and community work together to create a warm, welcoming and inclusive environment where everyone belongs. Togetherness helps children feel safe, supported and proud to be part of our school family.
Living Our Values Every Day
Our values are not simply words displayed on a wall: they are lived and experienced every day in classrooms, playgrounds, worship, learning and relationships across the school.
They influence how we treat one another, how we approach learning, and how we contribute to our community. Through our LIGHT values, we help children grow into confident, compassionate, and responsible young people who are ready to make a positive contribution to society.
Together, our values help bring our mission to life:
“We stand united in faith with the courage to build a loving world of truth, justice, peace and wisdom.”
At St John Fisher, we want every child to grow in faith, develop a lifelong love of learning and shine brightly in all they do.

Wraparound Provision
At St John Fisher Catholic Primary School, we understand that families need flexible childcare options to support busy working lives. Through our partnership with Simply Out of School St John Fisher, we provide high-quality wraparound care in a safe, welcoming and familiar environment for our pupils.
Simply Out of School offers both Breakfast Club and After School Club provision, giving children the opportunity to enjoy a positive start and finish to their school day. Based at St John Fisher, children are cared for in a familiar setting where they can relax, socialise and take part in a range of activities with friends.
Our Breakfast Club provides children with a calm and enjoyable start to the day before they begin their learning. Children can spend time with friends, take part in activities and prepare for the school day ahead.
After school, children can enjoy a variety of activities, creative opportunities and time to play in a relaxed environment. The provision allows children to continue developing friendships, build confidence and enjoy experiences beyond the classroom.
We work closely with Simply Out of School to ensure that the wraparound provision complements the values and ethos of St John Fisher. Through this partnership, families can feel confident that their children are welcomed, supported and cared for before and after the school day.
For more information about bookings, fees and availability, please visit the Simply Out of School St John Fisher website page.

Religious Education Curriculum
At St John Fisher Catholic Primary School, Religious Education is at the very heart of school life. Through faith-filled teaching, prayer, reflection and lived experiences, we help children grow in their relationship with God and develop a deeper understanding of themselves, others and the world around them.
Inspired by our mission:
“We stand united in faith with the courage to build a loving world of truth, justice, peace and wisdom,”
we nurture children spiritually, morally, socially and academically so that they may flourish as compassionate and confident members of God’s family.
We believe that Religious Education is far more than a subject taught in lessons: it is a way of living. Faith is woven throughout daily school life and helps shape the values, relationships and experiences that define our community.
Our Religious Education Curriculum
At St John Fisher, we follow the Lighting the Path Religious Education programme, developed to support children in growing in knowledge, understanding and lived faith.
This curriculum enables children to:
Through engaging lessons, meaningful discussion, prayer, scripture, music, art and reflection, children are encouraged to think deeply and make connections between faith and everyday life.
Grow in compassion, wisdom and responsibility
What Children Learn
The Religious Education curriculum is carefully planned to help children progressively develop their understanding of:
Scripture and the Life of Jesus
Children learn about key stories from the Bible and the teachings of Jesus, exploring how these continue to guide our lives today.
Pupils experience different forms of prayer and reflection and are encouraged to develop their own personal relationship with God.
Sacraments and Catholic Life
Children learn about the sacraments, liturgical seasons, Church traditions and what it means to live as part of a Catholic community.
Catholic Social Teaching
Inspired by Gospel values, pupils learn about justice, compassion, dignity, stewardship and how faith calls us to care for others and the world around us.
Other Faiths and Worldviews
We encourage children to value diversity and respect people of all faiths and backgrounds, promoting understanding and dialogue in an increasingly diverse world.
Learning Through Faith
Children’s Religious Education experiences extend beyond the classroom through:
At St John Fisher, we want every child to leave us with a secure understanding of their faith, a strong moral foundation, and the confidence to live with kindness, courage and hope.
Prayer and liturgy
Celebration of feast days and liturgical seasons
Parish links and sacramental preparation
Charity fundraising and social action
Pupil leadership opportunities

Our Governors
The Governing Body of St John Fisher Catholic Primary School plays a vital role in supporting the strategic leadership and continued development of our school. Working closely with the Headteacher and senior leaders, governors help ensure that every child receives the very best education within a caring, ambitious, and faith-filled environment.
As a Catholic school, our governors are committed to supporting the mission and values that shape life at St John Fisher:
“We stand united in faith with the courage to build a loving world of truth, justice, peace and wisdom.”
Governors work in partnership with school leaders to uphold our Catholic ethos, maintain high standards, and ensure that all children are supported to flourish academically, spiritually, socially, and emotionally.
What Do Governors Do?
The role of the Governing Body is strategic rather than operational. Governors work to:
Governors regularly visit the school, meet with leaders, and review key aspects of school improvement to ensure children receive a high-quality education and positive school experience.
Monitor educational standards and pupil outcomes
Our Commitment
At St John Fisher, we are fortunate to have a committed Governing Body made up of individuals who bring a wide range of skills, knowledge, and experience to their role. United by a shared commitment to our children, community, and Catholic values, governors work hard to support the continued success and development of our school.
We value the strong partnership between governors, school leaders, staff, parents, parish, and the wider community, recognising that children achieve their very best when we work together.

School Uniform
At St John Fisher Catholic Primary School, we believe that wearing school uniform promotes a sense of pride, belonging, equality and identity within our Catholic community. Our uniform helps pupils feel part of the school family, supports high expectations and ensures children are dressed comfortably and appropriately for learning.
We aim to keep our uniform affordable, practical and inclusive for families. Most items can be purchased from a range of retailers, with only a small number of school-specific items available through the school office.
Our School Uniform
Everyday Uniform
All pupils should wear:
White shirt with school tie or
Blue school jumper or cardigan with school logo
Grey trousers, pinafore dress or grey skirt
School Tie
Our blue and yellow striped tie should be worn when pupils are wearing a shirt.
Long-sleeved shirts should be worn during:
Short-sleeved shirts should be worn during:
Pupils wearing a white polo shirt are not required to wear a tie.
Summer Uniform
During the Summer Term, pupils may wear:
Yellow checked summer dress
Socks and Tights
P.E. Kit
Children should come to school wearing their P.E. kit on their allocated PE days.
P.E. Uniform
Plain (free from logos) navy blue tracksuit bottoms and sweatshirt/hoodie (for colder weather).
Suitable trainers for physical activity
Pupils should wear a white T-shirt with either navy shorts or a navy tracksuit, depending on the season and weather.
Forest School
Forest School Uniform
Pupils must wear long-sleeved tops and bottoms so that they are appropriate dressed to carry out the Forest School activities.
Long-sleeved navy top
Hair and Appearance
To maintain a smart, safe and practical appearance for learning:
Long hair should be tied back.
Hair bows, bands and clips should be plain blue or yellow (school colours).
Hair accessories should be modest in size and should not cover the face or interfere with learning.
Hair accessories should be suitable for school and practical for the school day.
Extreme hairstyles, shaved patterns or brightly coloured hair are not permitted.
Jewellery
Jewellery should not be worn unless required for religious practice or belief.
Stud earrings only may be worn.
Earrings must be removed for P.E. lessons for health and safety reasons.
School Coats
Children should bring a suitable coat to school during colder or wet weather.
We ask that coats are plain navy blue or black where possible, helping to maintain a smart appearance across the school.
Suitable for outdoor play and changing weather conditions
Practical and safe for school use
Free from large logos or inappropriate images or slogans
Families are not required to purchase a branded school coat and may buy suitable coats from any retailer.
Purchasing Uniform
The following items are available to purchase from the school office:
School logo jumper or cardigan
All other uniform items may be purchased from a retailer of your choice, provided they meet the school’s colour and uniform expectations.
We encourage all pupils to wear their uniform with pride and thank parents and carers for their support in maintaining high standards across our school community.
